summary: This note describes the Oktibbeha County School District in Mississippi, which operated schools serving Maben, Sturgis, and rural communities outside the Starkville City School District. It covers the district's West and East school campuses, its two state takeovers for academic failure and mismanagement, and the 2013 state law requiring consolidation into the Starkville School District. It also notes that East Oktibbeha Elementary was closed during the merger because its location would have produced a school over 90% black.
one_line: Former Mississippi school district serving Maben, Sturgis and rural Oktibbeha County, merged into Starkville schools after a 2013 state law.
key_facts: The Oktibbeha County School District served most of Maben and the town of Sturgis.
The West Oktibbeha County Elementary (Pre-K-6) and High Schools (7-12) served western parts of the county not in the Starkville City School District.
The East Oktibbeha County Elementary (K-6) and High Schools (7-12) served eastern parts of Oktibbeha County not included in the Starkville City School District.
The Oktibbeha County School District was taken over by the state twice due to academic failure and mismanagement.
The state proposed several times that the Oktibbeha County School District should be merged with the Starkville School District (SSD).
In 2013, the Mississippi Legislature passed a bill requiring that all Oktibbeha County schools be merged into the Starkville School District.
East Oktibbeha Elementary was closed during implementation of the merger.
East Oktibbeha Elementary was closed because its location would have resulted in a school that was over 90% black.
